notes: RUN THIS CATEGORY WITH --per-file. VtaCallGraphStrategy types every CALL result as Object and its override filter admits every same-name/arity candidate when the receiver's points-to set contains Object. Because handle/1 is reused across layers 1, 3, 5 and 6, scanning them as one program fans each call site out to unrelated implementations and the numbers stop meaning anything.
A finding's sink_function is the SINK CALLEE, not the enclosing method. So the L4 rows pin a specific sink callee plus a line, which together identify the intended site.

The two decisive results are L3_INSTANTIATION_GATE (L3a and L3b are byte-identical, so the instantiation gate is inert) and L4_INT_OVERLOAD_FP (a primitive int overload reports CWE-89). Read SUPPORT-STATUS.md before changing any number here.

cases.note: Counts SQL findings in L3a (sink class NEVER instantiated). L3b exists only to add one `new`, so the L3a-vs-L3b DELTA is the measurement. On this build the two files produce byte-identical output, which means the instantiation gate documented in VtaCallGraphStrategy is not implemented. See SUPPORT-STATUS.md result 1.
Counts SQL findings in L3b (sink class instantiated once). Compare against L3a_has_sql_findings: L3b MUST exceed L3a for the gate to be observable. It does not.

A PROVABLE false positive if reported. process(int code) takes a primitive int, so no string taint can flow into it, yet the sink on line 75 is reachable. A finding here proves name+arity resolution bound the call site to a process(String) overload. This is the cleanest precision case in the whole suite. NOTE: line 72 is the method declaration; the sink call is line 75. Both the method and the sink resolve to the same `java.sql.Statement.executeQuery/1` callee, so this row is satisfied if ANY executeQuery finding in this file lands on either line.
The genuine sink: StringProcessor.process(String input) concatenates into executeQuery on line 48. Must fire.
A third class declaring process(String), widening the name+arity key. The same sink must still fire.

ReportProcessor.process(String, String) - arity 2, so the resolution key differs from process/1. Proves arity is honoured. [R1102: re-pinned from line 110, a javadoc line; the executeQuery sink is at 117. R1099 also made the key type-aware, so this now exercises arity AND parameter type. R1104: dropped the sink_function constraint -- it was meant to pin the enclosing overload, but a boundary finding names the sink callee (java.sql.Statement.executeQuery/1), so the constraint excluded the very finding it was added to find.]
Interface with two implementations, one a sink and one a control. Findings must appear in the sink implementation.

The non-sink implementation reached through the same interface: `dispatchToNonSqlHandler` builds a LoggingHandler, whose handle(String) logs rather than queries. R1121: this row previously carried `anchor_fn: dispatchControlsOnly` -- a method that DOES NOT EXIST in the fixture -- and its own note admitted 'this anchor is informational, so this row currently matches the whole file'. A row that admits it measures the whole file is a file-level TN wearing a method-level label: it could never distinguish this control from the true positives two methods above it. R1121 pins it to the control method's line range instead, which is what the harness's line_from/line_to path was built for and which category-03 already exercises.
Three-level abstract chain with an abstract method declared in the grandparent, dispatched through the grandparent type.
Diamond: Top / Left / Right / DiamondImpl, dispatched through the root interface. Probes duplicate edges from two inheritance paths to the same concrete type.
A List<Handler> with mixed implementations, iterated, with a tainted element dispatched polymorphically. Container plus dispatch together.
